assign.outcome:
**The paging realm now teaches before it demonstrates — and the size chips finally change size.**

![the hub at 1280](/framework/ai/2026-09-04/paging-clarity/shots/hub-1280.jpg)

**1 · [The hub](/imagine/paging/) teaches in one screen.** Its toolbar and its five-stop walk of bare links are gone. It opens with what a page is, in plain sentences, then each of the four mechanisms under its own takeaway sentence with a **live miniature you click right there**: `swap` as a tab set (`ext/tabs`' own strip), `launch` as a pane opening beside a list that keeps its track, `expand` as a `ui/accordion`, `takeover` as three panes collapsing into a crumb strip. Then three numbered steps saying where to go next. Proved at 1280: the tab panel's top-left is identical before and after a click (532/246) while its text changes; launch 1 pane → 2 with the list unmoved; takeover 3 panes → 1 + 2 crumbs, and a crumb click restores all three.

**2 · [Sizes](/imagine/paging/sizes/) mean size.** The owner's bug was real, and both halves were measured live on the same page — the shipped `sample()` was reinstalled on the prototype, driven, then the new one restored and driven again (1920):

| chip | BEFORE — height · first words | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| `s` | 231px · "One line, and a way out of it." | 270px · "What does a click do? Four answers…" |
| `m` | 255px · "A page is an icon…" | 412px · same first words |
| `l` | 359px · "Sizes A page is an icon…" | 631px · same first words |
| `xl` | 471px · "01 A wall is what a column word is FOR…" | 928px · same first words |

Does the `s` line survive into the higher rungs? **Before: no, no, no. After: yes, yes, yes.** Every rung now KEEPS everything the rungs below it showed. And every demo box grew a caption that says what just changed: *"content: s → l. The box grew from 270px tall to 631px — 361px more, same width. Nothing was taken away."* Layout chips read the same way (`column → full`: 674 × 954 → 1858 × 804).

**3 · [Examples](/imagine/paging/examples/) show the result beside the configuration.** Five pages, each changing exactly ONE word from the one above it, each with the live box on the left and the `new Paging({…})` plus the three `page.pick(…)` lines on the right — **derived from the live page**, so the snippet cannot drift from the picture. Zero overflow on all ten snippets.

**4 · Real things as content.** `l` is four cards in the `ui/` card template verbatim; `xl` adds the blog's own posts in core's own card wall. A table on the hub says which built part appears where, with links (`ext/tabs`, `ui/accordion`, `ui/card`, `previews()`, the blog manifest, `styles/layouts/cols`, `ui/table`, the page generator — and `ext/Panel`, listed honestly as not used, with the reason).

**5 · [Make](/imagine/paging/make/) — dynamic pages, temporary persistence, RESET.** Real pages at real urls, grown at runtime from one string of text, reusing the page generator's own `parse()`/`serialize()` rather than a second tree-from-spec. Full CRUD, proved: Add "Reading list" → a row at `/imagine/paging/make/reading-list/`; a word click turned `Notes: card m launch` into `Notes: tint m launch`; `+` nested a child; `×` deleted a page and its subtree (7 rows → 3).

**RESET, proved.** Three changes on three pages (`sizes` content=xl, `styles` style=dark, a sixth page under `make`) → three keys under `lew42:paging:` → arm, confirm → **zero** keys, `make` back to its baseline five, `sizes` back to `m`/412px, `styles` back to `plain`. A second run planted `lew42:/imagine/team/` and `lew42:/notes/` first: both survived.

**The CRUD decision, in one line:** not `EditablePage extends Page` — the thing being edited is the TREE, which is the text, so CRUD is a PART (`Make`) over one spec string; a subclass would put persistence on every page to serve an operation that belongs to the tree's owner, and would still write back to the text to survive a reload. Contract and reasoning in [doc/decisions.md](/imagine/paging/doc/decisions.md).

**6 · Every page in the realm opens with its takeaway sentence** — 30 of them, `Paging.lede()` for the `Paging` pages and a marked `md()` for the four plain ones.

**Checked:** 148 page-widths (the hub and every page in the realm at 400/1280/1920/3440) — **zero** console errors, zero horizontal overflow, no Material Icons miss, every page carrying its lede.

**Left open, with reasons.** *Should a mode be shareable?* It is `localStorage` per url, which is honest but means a look you like is not a link you can send — a query string would fix it and would be the first state-in-a-url on this site; **the owner's call** ([persistence.md](/imagine/paging/doc/persistence.md)). *A page deleted under `make/` while its column is open stays on screen until you navigate* — core does not unmount a column it was not asked to, and reaching into the Router from a demo is the wrong fence. *A private-mode session is kept in core's in-memory fallback map*, which is not reachable from here — RESET's reload is what restores the demos there, not the clear.

log.msg: PROPOSALS for core/ and ext/ (nothing was edited outside the fence). (1) core/Page/Page.class.js - Page.Store has a module-level `memory` Map it falls back to when localStorage throws, and nothing outside that file can reach it; a realm-wide RESET therefore cannot clear a private-mode session. Proposed: a static `Page.Store.forget(prefix)` that clears BOTH the matching localStorage keys and the matching `memory` entries, returning the count. /imagine/paging/ would drop its own loop and call it. (2) ext/tabs/tabs.css - `.tab-panel { padding-top: 3em }` is a constant, sized for a full page's rhythm; a 200px embedded tab set has to override it with a rule of its own (the paging hub's `.paging-tabsdemo .tab-panel`). Proposed: `padding-top: var(--tab-gap, 3em)`, so an embedded set sets one token instead of writing a selector. (3) core/Page - a page removed from its parent's `children` while its column is open stays on screen until the next navigation; core has no seam to say 'this page is gone, drop its column'. /imagine/paging/make/ documents it as a known limit. Proposed: a `Page.drop(name)` that removes the child AND asks the Router to deactivate anything at or under its url. All three are small and none is needed for what landed today.
